$comment: CESIDR canonical statuses: draft canonical IDs for the categories into which the Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches sorts the Churches sui iuris. Referenced from data/churches.json as the value of each Church's `canonical_status` field. The CCEO defines four (can. 55-150, 151-154, 155-173, 174-176); the fifth entry here, cstat:latin, is not a CCEO category at all and exists because the Latin Church is governed by the 1983 Code of Canon Law instead — it is flagged with `cceo_category: false`. Status is an attribute and not identity: a Church raised from metropolitan sui iuris to major archiepiscopal keeps its `esi:` ID (schema proposal, rule 2). All IDs are drafts pending committee review; the `cstat:` prefix is a placeholder.

entries.governing_body: synod of bishops of the patriarchal Church
entries.note: The fullest developed form of an Eastern Catholic Church. The synod of bishops of the patriarchal Church is alone competent to make laws for the whole Church (can. 110 §1) and is its tribunal (§2); administrative acts belong to the patriarch, not the synod, unless the patriarch determines otherwise or common law reserves them to the synod (§4). The patriarch's power is validly exercised only within the territory of the patriarchal Church, unless the nature of the matter or law approved by the Roman Pontiff establishes otherwise (can. 78 §2). Patriarchs precede all bishops of any degree everywhere in the world, with due regard for special norms of precedence established by the Roman Pontiff (can. 58).

entries.governing_body: synod of bishops of the major archiepiscopal Church
entries.note: Governed by a major archbishop with his synod. Can. 152 assimilates it to a patriarchal Church in law, unless the common law expressly provides otherwise or it is evident from the nature of the matter. Two differences follow: the elected major archbishop must petition the Roman Pontiff for confirmation of his election (can. 153 §2), where a patriarchal election is only notified to him (can. 76 §1); and the worldwide precedence of patriarchs over all bishops (can. 58) does not extend to major archbishops, who instead take precedence of honour immediately after the patriarchs, in the order in which their Churches were erected as major archiepiscopal (can. 154).
Presided over by the metropolitan of a determined see, appointed by the Roman Pontiff and assisted by a council of hierarchs rather than by a synod (can. 155 §1).

The residual category, which the CCEO does not give a positive name — it is literally 'the other Churches sui iuris'. Each is entrusted to a hierarch who presides over it according to common law and the particular law established by the Roman Pontiff (can. 174); these Churches depend immediately on the Apostolic See, as whose delegate the hierarch exercises the rights and obligations of can. 159 nn. 3-8 (can. 175). The eight Churches in this category vary widely: some have an eparchy, some an apostolic exarchate or administration, and some no hierarchy of their own at all.

Not a CCEO category. The Latin Church is governed by the 1983 Code of Canon Law and headed by the Roman Pontiff directly, so none of the four Eastern categories applies to it. Whether it should instead be classed as patriarchal — the title Patriarch of the West having been restored to the Annuario Pontificio in 2024 after being dropped in 2006 — is open question 4 in docs/schema-proposal.md.
